description.ncbi_summary: Cytosolic and membrane-bound forms of glutathione S-transferase are encoded by two distinct supergene families. These enzymes function in the detoxification of electrophilic compounds, including carcinogens, therapeutic drugs, environmental toxins and products of oxidative stress, by conjugation with glutathione. The genes encoding these enzymes are known to be highly polymorphic. These genetic variations can change an individual's susceptibility to carcinogens and toxins as well as affect the toxicity and efficacy of some drugs. At present, eight distinct classes of the soluble cytoplasmic mammalian glutathione S-transferases have been identified: alpha, kappa, mu, omega, pi, sigma, theta and zeta. This gene encodes a glutathione S-tranferase belonging to the alpha class. The alpha class genes, located in a cluster mapped to chromosome 6, are the most abundantly expressed glutathione S-transferases in liver. In addition to metabolizing bilirubin and certain anti-cancer drugs in the liver, the alpha class of these enzymes exhibit glutathione peroxidase activity thereby protecting the cells from reactive oxygen species and the products of peroxidation. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Glutathione S-transferase involved in the clearance of a variety of electrophilic toxic compounds by glutathione conjugation, including harmful products generated during oxidative stress and xenobiotics such as environmental toxins, drugs, and carcinogens including derivatives of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PubMed:10395737, PubMed:12067250, PubMed:15077012, PubMed:28478157). Catalyzes the nucleophilic attack of the sulfur atom of glutathione on the electrophilic groups of a wide range of substrates (PubMed:10395737, PubMed:12067250, PubMed:15077012, PubMed:28478157). Involved in the protection from oxidative stress through its glutathione-dependent peroxidase activity toward lipid hydroperoxides, including linoleic acid hydroperoxides, dilinoleoyl phosphatidylcholine hydroperoxide, and dilinoleoyl phosphatidylethanolamine hydroperoxide (PubMed:10395737). Can also catalyze glutathione conjugation with 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), a toxic product of lipid peroxidation (PubMed:10395737). Is involved in the protection from toxic effects of bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) on male fertility through the activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway (By similarity). In vitro, it catalyzes the reduction of cumene hydroperoxide (PubMed:10395737, PubMed:15077012).
